# core


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

This module holds everything fossick does with a single URL or file.
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch)
downloads a page and
[`to_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#to_md) turns
its HTML into markdown.
[`crawl`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#crawl) follows
links from one page to the next.
[`find_xhr`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#find_xhr)
and
[`paginate_api`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#paginate_api)
find the JSON API a page loads its data from and read it directly.
Separate readers handle arXiv papers, GitHub repositories, YouTube
videos and PDFs, and
[`read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read), at the
end of the notebook, picks the right one for any target.

### syncy

``` python
def syncy(
    coro, tout:int=60
):
```

*Run the coroutine `coro` from ordinary synchronous code and return its
result; on timeout, cancel it and raise `TimeoutError`.*

``` python
#: a timeout cancels the work and says it may already have happened; the coroutine's own `TimeoutError` passes through unchanged
async def _own(): raise TimeoutError('inner')
try: syncy(_own())
except TimeoutError as e: assert str(e) == 'inner'
else: raise AssertionError('no error')
async def _slow(): await asyncio.sleep(5)
try: syncy(_slow(), tout=0.1)
except TimeoutError as e: assert 'cancelled' in str(e) and 'may already' in str(e)
else: raise AssertionError('no timeout')
```

## Turning HTML into markdown

A downloaded page is mostly markup that a reader does not need:
navigation bars, scripts, styles and advertisements.
[`to_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#to_md) strips
that away and returns the text as markdown. It accepts either a raw HTML
string or a response returned by
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch), and
with `sel` it converts only the part of the page that matches a CSS
selector, such as `sel='article'`.
[`html2md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#html2md)
does the same for a string alone, and
[`html_title`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#html_title)
returns a document’s title.

### html_title

``` python

    s:str

```

*Return the text of the document’s `<title>`, or of its first `<h1>`
when it has no title, or an empty string.*

By default
[`to_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#to_md) and
[`html2md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#html2md) run
[readability](https://github.com/buriy/python-readability), the article
extractor behind browser reading modes. It finds the main article and
drops everything around it, which is what you want for a page fetched
from the web. It can also drop parts of a document you meant to keep,
such as section headings. For a page someone saved on purpose, or a
local HTML file, pass `readability=False`. The whole document is then
converted, and only scripts, styles, `noscript` and `template` blocks
and HTML comments are removed. The test below shows readability losing
two `<h3>` headings that `readability=False` keeps.

## Downloading pages

### Refusing private addresses

A program that fetches URLs chosen by an AI agent can be made to fetch
addresses inside your own network. Examples are a router’s admin page
and a cloud server’s metadata service, which hands out credentials. This
attack is called server-side request forgery.
[`check_url`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#check_url)
refuses any URL that is not http or https. It refuses host names such as
`localhost` and `metadata.google.internal`. It refuses any host that
resolves to a private, loopback, link-local or other non-public address.
It raises
[`BlockedURL`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#blockedurl).
The message names two ways to allow such a URL. Pass
`allow_private=True` to one call, or set the environment variable
`FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1` for the whole process.
[`get_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_page),
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch),
`http_get` and `http_post` run this check first.
[`http_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#http_page)
does not.

The check looks up the host name, and then the download looks it up
again. The two lookups can get different answers. A person who controls
the DNS for a name can give a public address to the check and
`127.0.0.1` to the download. This attack is called DNS rebinding. To
stop it, the plain HTTP path of
[`get_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_page)
gives libcurl the addresses that the check approved, with the libcurl
option `CURLOPT_RESOLVE`. libcurl then connects only to those addresses
and does not look up the name again. The plain path also follows
redirects itself. Before it connects to a new URL, it checks and pins
the address of that URL in the same way. It does not send cookies,
`auth` or credential headers that you supplied to a different host.

Some paths cannot pin the address, and keep only the first check.
Through a proxy, also one that is set in the environment, the proxy
looks up the name. The browser paths (`heavy`, `stealthy`, `session`,
and `auto=True` after the plain step) check only the first URL. The
browser does its own lookups, follows redirects, and loads scripts and
images from other addresses with no check. For URLs that you do not
trust, use the plain path.

### Downloading one page

[`get_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_page)
runs
[`check_url`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#check_url),
then downloads the page in one of four ways. By default it sends a plain
HTTP request. `heavy=True` loads the page in a headless browser so that
its JavaScript runs. `stealthy=True` uses scrapling’s stealth browser,
which is built to pass bot checks such as Cloudflare’s. `session=True`
uses the logged-in Chrome described in `fossick.cdp`, with its cookies.
The browsers load on first use. When they cannot load,
[`get_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_page)
raises
[`BrowserUnavailable`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#browserunavailable).

`http_get` and `http_post` are
[`get_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_page)
with the method set and a 30 second timeout. All of them verify TLS
certificates by default. Pass `verify=False` only for a host you trust
that has a bad certificate.
[`http_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#http_page)
sends a plain request with GET, POST, PUT or DELETE and skips the
address check. Use
[`http_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#http_page)
only for URLs your own code chose. Most callers need
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch), below.

Two optional limits apply to the plain path. `max_bytes` stops the
download when the body becomes larger than that number of bytes, and
raises
[`TooLarge`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#toolarge).
A server that sends gigabytes then cannot fill the memory before
[`to_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#to_md) runs.
`max_recv_speed` sets the highest download speed, in bytes per second.
Both limits are off by default. The browser paths do not use them.
[`http_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#http_page)
also takes `max_bytes`, and `curl_options` for other libcurl options.

Some networks inspect TLS traffic with their own root certificate.
curl_cffi does not use the system keychain, so on such a machine a check
of the certificate fails with
`curl: (60) ... unable to get local issuer certificate`. Give the plain
path a CA bundle file that holds the normal roots and the inspection
root. Pass `ca_bundle=` or `verify=` with the path of the file, or set
one of the environment variables `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` or
`REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`. fossick reads them in that order, on each request.
It uses the first one that names a file. On macOS, when none of these is
set, fossick uses the system keychain. It reads the certificates of the
system keychains once with `security find-certificate`, adds them to
certifi’s roots, and keeps the result in its cache folder for one day.
An inspection root that your company put in the system keychain then
works with no setup. The bundle applies only when verification is on:
with `verify=True`, as `http_get` sets it, or with `ca_bundle=`. fossick
never turns verification off. On other systems, when none of these is
set, nothing changes.

### [`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch)

Most code downloads a page with
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch). It
wraps
[`get_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_page)
and returns scrapling’s response object with two attributes added.
`html` holds the page, or only the part matching `sel`. `xhr` holds the
background requests recorded when `capture_xhr=True`. The response also
has `status`, `url`, and a `json()` method for JSON replies.

`auto=True` tries the download methods in turn: plain HTTP, then the
headless browser, then the stealth browser, then the stealth browser
through the logged-in Chrome. A bot wall is a page that asks for a
verification step instead of showing the requested content. `auto=True`
stops at the first response that is not a bot wall. It records the
method that worked in `tier`, or `'blocked'` if none did. It records
each failed attempt and its reason in `errs`.

[`browser_session`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#browser_session)
downloads many pages with one browser. Starting a browser takes seconds.
[`browser_session`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#browser_session)
opens one browser for the length of a `with` block and gives you a
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch)-like
function that reuses it.

`auto=True` can end in the logged-in Chrome. That last method connects
to the debug Chrome on port 9223, starts it if it is not running, and
sends the cookies that Chrome has for the site. This is correct for a
page that you want to read as yourself. It is not correct for a URL that
comes from a web page, a document or another person. Such a URL can make
your logged-in browser open a page with your cookies. When you do not
trust the URL, pass `auto=False`. This is the default for
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch), but not
for [`read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read). With
`auto=False`, and without `heavy`, `stealthy`, `session` or
`capture_xhr`, no function in this module starts a browser or connects
to port 9223. This includes
[`get_pdf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_pdf) and
its proof-of-work step,
[`read_arxiv`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#read_arxiv),
[`read_gh_file`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#read_gh_file),
[`crawl`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#crawl) and
[`read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read). The
plain path always checks redirects: `follow_redirects` is `'safe'` by
default, and fossick checks and pins each step itself. The section
*Fetching untrusted URLs*, near the end of this notebook, tests this.

### fetch

``` python
def fetch(
    url:str, # URL to fetch
    sel:str=None, # CSS selector to extract (None = full page)
    method:str='GET', # HTTP method; 'POST' sends payload as JSON body
    payload:dict=None, # POST body (JSON) or GET query params
    heavy:bool=False, # Full JS rendering via headless browser
    stealthy:bool=False, # Anti-bot stealth fetcher (Cloudflare etc.)
    capture_xhr:bool=False, # Capture XHR calls made by the page (only works with heavy or stealthy)
    session:bool=False, # Route through the persistent debug Chrome (reuses its logged-in cookies); True or a port int
    auto:bool=False, # Try plain, heavy, stealthy, then the logged-in debug Chrome with its cookies for the site; keep False for untrusted URLs
    allow_private:bool=None, # Allow localhost/intranet targets (default: refuse; $FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1)
    max_bytes:int=None, # Plain HTTP only: raise `TooLarge` when the body is larger than this many bytes (default: no limit)
    max_recv_speed:int=None, # Plain HTTP only: the highest download speed, in bytes per second (default: no limit)
    **kw
)->scrapling.engines.toolbelt.custom.Response: # Extra kwargs passed to scrapling (e.g. verify, headers, timeout)
```

*Download `url` and return the response with `.html` set to the page, or
the part matching `sel`, and `.xhr` set to any recorded background
requests. `auto=True` can end in the logged-in debug Chrome, so pass
`auto=False` for untrusted URLs.*

### Bot walls

Many sites put a challenge page in front of their content for visitors
they think are scripts. Cloudflare’s “Just a moment” page and the Anubis
proof-of-work page are common examples. The challenge often arrives with
status 200, so it looks like a successful download. fossick treats a
response as blocked when its status is 401, 403, 429, 503 or 530, when
its HTML contains the marker of a known challenge or captcha widget, or
when it is a 200 response with less than 200 characters of HTML. The
tests below check these rules, including that a page which only mentions
the word captcha is not counted as blocked.

The cells after that run against real sites and are not run by the
tests. They show a Cloudflare and an Anubis wall being detected,
`auto=True` stopping at the plain tier for a page that needs nothing
more,
[`browser_session`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#browser_session)
reusing one browser for two pages, and `session=True` going through the
logged-in Chrome.

``` python
# A site behind Cloudflare: a plain fetch hits the bot wall, and _blocked() flags it for escalation
cf = fetch('https://www.scrapingcourse.com/cloudflare-challenge', verify=False)
assert cf.status == 403, f'expected a Cloudflare 403 challenge, got {cf.status}'
assert _blocked(cf) is True            # fetch(auto=True) escalates from here (heavy -> stealthy -> session)
print('cloudflare:', cf.status, '| blocked?', _blocked(cf))
```

``` python
# A site behind Anubis (proof-of-work bot wall): _blocked() now recognizes it, so fetch(auto=True) escalates
an = fetch('https://anubis.techaro.lol/', verify=False)
assert 'making sure' in an.html.lower(), 'expected the Anubis challenge page'
assert _blocked(an) is True            # Anubis markers are in _BLOCK_MARKERS -> auto escalates past this wall
print('anubis wall detected by _blocked?', _blocked(an))
```

``` python
# regression: a normal page that merely *mentions* captcha must NOT read as a bot wall.
# Wikipedia embeds hCaptcha config keys in its page JS -- the word is there, but there's no challenge widget.
wiki = fetch('https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anubis', verify=False)
assert wiki.status == 200 and 'captcha' in wiki.html.lower()   # the word IS present on the page...
assert _blocked(wiki) is False   # ...but _BLOCK_MARKERS matches captcha *widgets* (g-recaptcha/h-captcha/...), not the word
```

``` python
# fetch(auto=True): walks plain->heavy->stealthy->session, stops at the first unblocked tier, tags .tier
plain = fetch('https://example.com', auto=True, verify=False)
assert plain.status == 200 and plain.tier == 'plain'   # a static page needs no escalation
print('example.com ->', plain.tier)
```

``` python
# browser_session(): open ONE browser, reuse it across fetches (skips per-URL relaunch)
with browser_session() as bf:
    a = bf('https://example.com')
    b = bf('https://httpbin.org/html')
assert a.status == 200 and b.status == 200
assert len(a.html) > 0 and len(b.html) > 0
```

``` python
# fetch(session=True): route through the persistent debug Chrome, reusing its logged-in cookies
pg = fetch('https://httpbin.org/headers', session=True)
assert pg.status == 200
print(pg.html[:200])
```

## Crawling and batches

[`crawl`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#crawl) visits
pages breadth-first, starting from one URL and following the links that
match `follow_sel`, until it has visited `max_pages` pages. By default
it stays on the starting site. It returns the responses that came back
with status 200, and a page that fails to download is reported and
skipped. `delay` waits between requests so as not to load a small site
heavily. For crawls with `heavy` or `stealthy`, one browser is kept open
for the whole crawl unless `reuse=False`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/cli.py#L45"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### crawl

``` python
def crawl(
    start_url:str, # URL to start from
    sel:str=None, # CSS selector to extract per page
    follow_sel:str='a[href]', # CSS selector for links to follow
    same_domain:bool=True, # Only follow links on same domain
    max_pages:int=10, # Max pages to visit
    delay:float=0, # Seconds to wait between requests (polite crawling)
    heavy:bool=False, # Full JS rendering via headless browser
    stealthy:bool=False, # Anti-bot stealth fetcher (Cloudflare etc.)
    reuse:bool=True, # For heavy/stealthy crawls, keep one browser open across pages
    **kw
)->list: # Extra kwargs passed to scrapling (e.g. verify, timeout)
```

*Visit pages breadth-first from `start_url`, following links that match
`follow_sel`, and return the responses that had status 200.*

[`fetch_all`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#fetch_all)
downloads a list of URLs you already have, in parallel threads, and
returns the responses in the same order.
[`get_options`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_options)
reads the choices out of a `<select>` drop-down, which is how many sites
list chapters, categories or years; the example uses a small page with
three options.

## PDFs and arXiv papers

[`get_pdf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_pdf)
downloads a PDF, or reads one from disk, and returns it as a
`PdfDocument` from [pdf_oxide](https://github.com/yfedoseev/pdf_oxide),
or None when the bytes are not a PDF. It checks for the `%PDF-`
signature in the first 1024 bytes of the content and ignores the URL.
arXiv serves papers from URLs with no `.pdf` ending. The NCBI PubMed
Central archive puts a small proof-of-work check in front of its PDFs.
When the reply is such a check,
[`get_pdf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_pdf)
solves it and downloads the PDF again with the answer. Any page can
contain the markers of this check, so the second download goes through
the plain path of
[`get_page`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_page),
with the same address and redirect checks, timeout and `max_bytes` as
the first. `max_bytes` limits the size of the PDF. When `save_path` is a
folder or a file name, it saves a copy of the file. The examples
download two papers from the Self-Determination Theory site and print
the start of their text.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/core.py#L542"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
    max_bytes:int=None, # raise `TooLarge` when the download is larger than this many bytes (default: no limit)
    **scrapling_kw
)->pdf_oxide.pdf_oxide.PdfDocument | None: # extra kwargs passed to `get_page` (e.g. verify, headers, timeout, allow_private)
```

*Download a PDF from a URL, or read one from disk, and return it as a
`PdfDocument`, or None when the bytes are not a PDF.*

[`read_arxiv`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#read_arxiv)
takes an arXiv URL, of either the abstract page or the PDF, or a bare id
such as `2306.14881`. It returns the paper’s `title`, `authors`,
`summary`, `published` date, `link`, `pdf_url` and `pdf_path`. By
default it also saves the PDF in `save_dir`. With `source=True` it adds
the full text of the paper as markdown under `source`. The metadata is
cached on disk. A second call for the same paper makes no request.
`force=True` fetches the metadata again.

``` python
    force:bool=False, # if True, forces re-download even if cached
    **kw
)->dict: # http_get kwargs (e.g. verify=False to skip SSL verification, headers=... etc.)
```

*Return an arXiv paper’s metadata and PDF path, and optionally its full

These functions turn documents into markdown or notebooks.
[`pdf2md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#pdf2md)
converts a PDF to one markdown string, with pages separated by `---`,
using [pdflite](https://github.com/vedicreader/pdflite). It saves images
from the PDF in an
[`images`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#images) folder
inside a folder named after `out_path`. This module re-exports pdflite’s
own functions, such as `pdf_md` and `clean_md`.
[`url2nb`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#url2nb) saves
a web page, PDF or arXiv paper as a Jupyter notebook.
[`pdf2nb`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#pdf2nb) saves
a PDF as a notebook. Both return the notebook’s path. Both skip the work
when the notebook already exists, unless `force=True`.


``` python
_c = _md2cells('# Intro\n\nSome prose.\n\n[code]\n\n> 1+1\n2\n[/code]\n\n## Next\n\nMore.')
assert [(c.cell_type, c.source) for c in _c] == [('markdown','# Intro\n\nSome prose.'), ('code','1+1\n# => 2'), ('markdown','## Next\n\nMore.')], _c
assert _md2cells('[code]\n\ndef f(x):\nreturn x\n[/code]')[0].source == 'def f(x):\n    return x'
_t = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()); Pdf.from_markdown('# Attention\n\nSome prose about attention.').save(str(_t/'a.pdf'))
_rf, fetch = fetch, lambda url, **kw: '<html><body><h1>Title</h1><p>' + 'Some prose about notebooks. '*20 + '</p></body></html>'
try: _hp = url2nb('https://example.com/page', nb_path=_t/'page.ipynb')
finally: fetch = _rf
assert 'Some prose about notebooks' in _hp.read_text()
_seen, _rp = [], pdf_md
def pdf_md(*a, **kw): _seen.append(kw.get('ocr')); return _rp(*a, **kw)
try: _pp = pdf2nb(str(_t/'a.pdf'), nb_path=_t/'attn.ipynb', ocr_selection='off')
finally: pdf_md = _rp
assert _seen == ['off'] and 'Attention' in _pp.read_text()
```

## GitHub

[`gh_clone`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#gh_clone)
returns a local copy of a repository. The first call clones it into
fossick’s cache folder, in a folder named `owner__repo`. It clones over
HTTPS only, and never asks for a password. Pass `ssh=True` to try SSH
after HTTPS, for a private repository and an SSH key. SSH then runs in
batch mode, so it fails at once when it needs a passphrase. The clone is
shallow: it gets only the latest commit. Pass `depth=None` for the full
history, or a different number of commits. `timeout` is the time limit
for each git command, in seconds. When git takes longer, fossick stops
git, removes the part-made folder and raises `TimeoutError`. Later calls
fetch the clone and reset it to the latest commit. Git runs with
`/dev/null` as stdin and never reads the caller’s terminal. fossick
gives git its own environment and does not change `os.environ`. fossick
refuses a target that starts with `-`, and puts `--` before the URL, so
that git cannot read a URL as an option.
[`gh_clone`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#gh_clone)
returns a local path unchanged. Code that accepts a repository therefore
accepts a folder on disk.
[`read_gh_repo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#read_gh_repo)
reads files from that clone and returns `{path: text}`. By default it
reads the README, `pyproject.toml` and every Python file. It caches its
results for an hour.
[`read_gh_file`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#read_gh_file)
downloads one file as raw text from its GitHub page URL. It returns
source code exactly as written. It converts the file to markdown only
when GitHub serves HTML.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/cli.py#L154"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### gh_clone

``` python
def gh_clone(
    path_or_url:str, # GitHub URL, SSH address, or a local path (returned as-is)
    depth:int=1, # commits of history to clone; None for all of them
    timeout:float=300, # seconds for each git command; then git is stopped and the part-made folder removed
    ssh:bool=False, # try SSH after HTTPS, for a private repo and an SSH key
)->pathlib.Path:
```

*Return a local clone of a GitHub repository, cloned or updated in
fossick’s cache, or return a local path unchanged.*

These tests give
[`gh_clone`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#gh_clone) a
fake `subprocess.run`, so they need no network. By default the clone is
HTTPS only and shallow, and `--` comes before the URL. A failed HTTPS
clone does not try SSH, because SSH can ask for a passphrase. With
`ssh=True`, SSH comes second and runs in batch mode. Git gets its own
environment, and `os.environ` stays the same. A clone that passes
`timeout` raises `TimeoutError` and leaves no folder. A target that
starts with `-` is refused before git runs.

``` python
from unittest.mock import patch
import uuid
```

``` python
_runs = []
def _fake_git(fail=(), slow=False):
    def run(cmd, **kw):
        _runs.append((cmd, kw))
        if cmd[1] == 'clone':
            d = Path(cmd[-1]); d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); (d/'half').write_text('x')
            if slow: raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(cmd, kw['timeout'])
            if any(f in cmd[-2] for f in fail): return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, 128, '', 'fatal: no access')
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, 0, '', '')
    return run

_url = f'https://github.com/fossick-test/{uuid.uuid4().hex}'
_d = _clone_dir(_gh_remotes(_url)[0])
_before = dict(os.environ)
with patch('subprocess.run', _fake_git(fail=('https://',))):
    test_fail(lambda: gh_clone(_url), contains='no access')
test_eq(len(_runs), 1)                                        # HTTPS only: no SSH fallback
cmd, kw = _runs[0]
test_eq(cmd, ['git', 'clone', '--depth', '1', '--', _gh_remotes(_url)[0], str(_d)])
test_eq(kw['env']['GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT'], '0'); test_eq(kw['timeout'], 300); test_eq(kw['stdin'], subprocess.DEVNULL)
assert not _d.exists()                                        # the failed clone left nothing behind
test_eq(dict(os.environ), _before)                            # os.environ is never changed

_runs.clear()
with patch('subprocess.run', _fake_git(fail=('https://',))): test_eq(gh_clone(_url, depth=None, ssh=True), _d)
test_eq([c[2:] for c, _ in _runs], [['--', _gh_remotes(_url)[0], str(_d)], ['--', _gh_remotes(_url, ssh=True)[1], str(_d)]])
assert _gh_remotes(_url, ssh=True)[1].startswith('git@github.com:')
assert 'BatchMode=yes' in _runs[1][1]['env']['GIT_SSH_COMMAND']
shutil.rmtree(_d)

_runs.clear()
with patch('subprocess.run', _fake_git(slow=True)): test_fail(lambda: gh_clone(_url, timeout=5), contains='more than 5')
test_eq(_runs[0][1]['timeout'], 5)
assert not _d.exists()                                        # stopped git, removed the part-made folder

_runs.clear()
with patch('subprocess.run', _fake_git()):
    test_fail(lambda: gh_clone('--upload-pack=touch /tmp/x'), contains='starts with "-"')
test_eq(_runs, [])
test_eq(_gh_remotes('git@github.com:a/b.git'), ['https://github.com/a/b.git'])   # an SSH address clones over HTTPS too
```

## Finding the API behind a page

Many modern pages arrive nearly empty. JavaScript then loads their data
with background requests, called XHR or fetch calls, which usually
return JSON. You can read that JSON directly instead of scraping the
rendered page.
[`find_xhr`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#find_xhr)
loads a page in a headless browser, records the background requests it
makes, and returns each one whose URL matches `pattern` as a dictionary
with `url`, `content_type` and the decoded `data`. With `session=True`
it records the requests through the logged-in Chrome instead, and each
result also carries a `capture`.
[`replay_xhr`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#replay_xhr)
sends a captured request again as a plain HTTP call with the browser’s
cookies. Use it to call an API that needs a login without keeping a
browser open.

`pattern` can be a regular expression, such as `.*products.*`, or a
shell-style glob, such as `*products*`.
[`compile_pattern`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#compile_pattern)
accepts both: it tries the text as a regular expression and, when that
is invalid, reads it as a glob.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/core.py#L881"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### replay_xhr

``` python
def replay_xhr(
    capture:dict, # a request dict from cdp.calls() or find_xhr(session=True)[i].capture
    data:NoneType=None, # override request body (str/dict); defaults to the captured body
    port:int=9223, # debug Chrome port to pull cookies from
    use_cookies:bool=True, # attach the browser's cookies for this domain (keeps auth)
    **kw
)->scrapling.engines.toolbelt.custom.Response: # Extra kwargs passed to the underlying Fetcher (headers, params, verify)
```

*Send a request captured from the browser again as a plain HTTP call,
with the debug Chrome’s cookies for that site.*

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/cli.py#L207"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
)->list: # Extra kwargs passed to fetch (verify, network_idle, etc.)
```

whose URLs match `pattern`.*

### compile_pattern

``` python
def compile_pattern(
    pattern
):
```

*Compile `pattern` as a regular expression, or as a shell-style glob
such as `*foo*` when it is not a valid one.*

``` python
assert compile_pattern('.*products.*').search('https://api.example.com/products?q=1')
assert compile_pattern('*products*').search('https://api.example.com/products?q=1')
assert not compile_pattern('*products*').search('https://api.example.com/search')
assert compile_pattern('.*[Ss]earch.*').search('https://api.example.com/Search')
```

An API rarely returns its records at the top level of the JSON. They
might be under `results`, or several levels down at
`data.products.items`.
[`json_records`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#json_records)
finds them by searching the whole payload for the longest list of
dictionaries, and `with_key=True` also tells you which key held it.

[`paginate_api`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#paginate_api)
reads every page of a paged JSON API. It sends the request repeatedly,
raising the page number in `page_field` each time, and stops when a page
comes back empty or shorter than the page size, or after `max_pages`
pages. It finds each page’s records with `results_field` if you name one
and
[`json_records`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#json_records)
if you do not. With `save=True` each page is written to a file, and a
later run reads the saved pages instead of fetching them again.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/cli.py#L224"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### paginate_api

``` python
def paginate_api(
    url:str, # API endpoint URL
    payload:dict=None, # Request body (POST) or params (GET)
    page_field:str='pageNumber', # Payload key to increment for each page
    size_field:str='pageSize', # Payload key for page size (detects last page)
    results_field:str=None, # Response key with items list (auto-detect if None)
    method:str='POST', # HTTP method
    max_pages:int=10, page_size:int=24, # Page size to request (only used if not in payload)
    page_start:int=1, # Starting page number (default 1)
    save:bool=False, # If True, saves each page's items to disk
    save_file:str='{url}_page_{page}.json', # Filepath pattern for saving (only used if save=True)
    force:bool=False, # If True, forces re-fetching even if saved file exists
    **kw
)->list: # Extra kwargs passed to fetch() (verify, headers, etc.)
```

*Request successive pages of a JSON API and return the items from every
page in one list.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/core.py#L905"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### json_records

``` python
def json_records(
    data, # any decoded JSON payload
    min_len:int=2, # shortest list of dicts worth calling records
    key:str=None, # only accept a list held under this key, at any depth
    with_key:bool=False, # also return the key the records were found under
    max_depth:int=6
):
```

*Return the longest list of dictionaries found anywhere in a decoded
JSON payload.*

[`download_files`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#download_files)
saves every file linked from a page whose link matches `pattern`, for
example `*.pdf` or `.*\.ipynb$`. With `follow=True` it first crawls from
the page, so it can collect files spread over a series of pages. Files
already on disk are not downloaded again unless `force=True`. The
example walks the JAX tutorial pages by their “next” links and saves
each notebook.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/core.py#L968"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### download_files

``` python
def download_files(
    url:str, pattern:str='*', # Glob or regex to match download hrefs
    save_dir:str='.', # Directory to save files
    follow:bool=False, # Crawl linked pages looking for more files
    follow_sel:str='a[href]', # Selector for page links to follow when crawling
    file_sel:str='a[href]', # Selector to scan for download links on each page
    same_domain:bool=True, max_pages:int=10, delay:float=0,
    force:bool=False, # Re-download even if file already exists
    heavy:bool=False, stealthy:bool=False, **kw
)->list[pathlib.Path]: # Extra kwargs passed to fetch/http_get (e.g. verify)
```

*Download every file linked from `url` whose link matches `pattern`,
optionally crawling linked pages first, and return the saved paths.*

``` python
jax, fs = 'https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/notebooks/thinking_in_jax.html', 'a[class="right-next"]'
download_files(jax, follow=True, follow_sel=fs, file_sel='a[href$=".ipynb"]', save_dir=sp, verify=False)
```

``` python
from fastcore.test import test_eq
```

``` python
_pages = crawl('https://lego.sankalpa.sh/', max_pages=2, verify=False)
assert isinstance(_pages, list), f"Expected list, got {type(_pages)}"
assert len(_pages) > 0, "Expected at least one page"
```

``` python
assert _jsp and all(p.status == 200 for p in _jsp)

```

``` python
# Step 1: visit the listing page with a headless browser, capture all XHR/fetch calls
apis = find_xhr('https://www.danmurphys.com.au/list/wine-all', verify=False)
```

``` python
# paginate_api: test with JSONPlaceholder (free public REST API, GET-based)
posts = paginate_api(
    'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts',
    payload={'_page': 1, '_limit': 5},
    page_field='_page',
    size_field='_limit',
    method='GET',
    verify=False,
)
assert len(posts) >= 5
assert 'title' in posts[0]
```

`find_xhr(session=True)` records requests through the logged-in Chrome,
so a request that needs your cookies can be captured and then replayed
with
[`replay_xhr`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#replay_xhr):

``` python
# find_xhr(session=True) -> replay_xhr: capture a request via the authenticated debug Chrome,
# then replay it as a fast plain-HTTP call using the browser's cookies
hits = find_xhr('https://httpbin.org/json', pattern='.*json', session=True)
assert hits, 'no matching request captured'
assert hits[0].capture, 'each hit should carry a replayable capture'
r = replay_xhr(hits[0].capture)
assert r.status == 200
print(hits[0].url, '->', r.status)
```

## YouTube

These three functions use [yt-dlp](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp).
[`search_yt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#search_yt)
searches YouTube and returns a list of result dictionaries.
[`read_yt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#read_yt)
returns one video’s details and its transcript under the key `source`.
The transcript comes from YouTube’s English automatic captions. A video
without them has an empty transcript. `read_yt(url, cues=True)` adds
`cues`, a list of `{start, end, text}` with times in seconds, so a
caller can seek to a line. `yt_link(url, seconds)` makes a watch link
that opens at that time.
[`read_yt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#read_yt)
caches results, cues included, on disk by video id.
[`download_yt`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#download_yt)
saves a video’s audio as mp3 or its video as mp4. The mp3 format needs
ffmpeg. All three accept `verify=False` to skip certificate checks. Use
it behind a proxy that rewrites HTTPS.

``` python
def read_yt(
```

The cue parser is tested on a saved YouTube caption sample, so no
network is needed. YouTube repeats each line in the next cue as the
caption rolls up. The parser folds the repeats, so each spoken line
shows once, with its start and end time.

``` python
from fastcore.test import test_eq, test_fail
```

``` python
_vtt = '''WEBVTT
Kind: captions
Language: en

00:00:00.160 --> 00:00:02.230 align:start position:0%
 
hello<00:00:00.640><c> and</c><00:00:00.880><c> welcome</c><00:00:01.440><c> to</c><00:00:01.600><c> the</c><00:00:01.760><c> show</c>

00:00:02.230 --> 00:00:02.240 align:start position:0%
hello and welcome to the show
 

00:00:02.240 --> 00:00:04.470 align:start position:0%
hello and welcome to the show
today<00:00:02.800><c> we</c><00:00:03.040><c> learn</c><00:00:03.520><c> about</c><00:00:03.919><c> neurons</c>

00:00:04.470 --> 00:00:04.480 align:start position:0%
today we learn about neurons
 

00:00:04.480 --> 00:00:07.109 align:start position:0%
today we learn about neurons
each<00:00:04.799><c> neuron</c><00:00:05.200><c> holds</c><00:00:05.600><c> a</c><00:00:05.759><c> number</c>

00:00:07.109 --> 00:00:07.119 align:start position:0%
each neuron holds a number
 

00:01:05.000 --> 00:01:07.500
that is all for today
'''
cues = _parse_cues(_vtt)
test_eq([c['text'] for c in cues], ['hello and welcome to the show','today we learn about neurons','each neuron holds a number','that is all for today'])
test_eq([(c['start'], c['end']) for c in cues][:2], [(0.16, 2.23), (2.24, 4.47)])
test_eq((cues[-1]['start'], cues[-1]['end']), (65.0, 67.5))
assert all(isinstance(c['start'], float) and isinstance(c['end'], float) for c in cues)
test_eq(_parse_cues(''), [])
test_eq(_parse_cues('WEBVTT\n\n'), [])
test_eq(' '.join(c['text'] for c in cues), _parse_vtt(_vtt))
```

``` python
test_eq(yt_link('https://youtu.be/aircAruvnKk?t=3', 83.9), 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aircAruvnKk&t=83s')
test_eq(yt_link('aircAruvnKk', 0), 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aircAruvnKk&t=0s')
test_fail(lambda: yt_link('not-an-id', 5), contains='video id')
test_fail(lambda: yt_link('aircAruvnKk/../x', 5), contains='video id')
```

``` python
# read_yt with a stubbed yt-dlp and fetch: cues kept in the cache, hidden by default
class _YDL:
    def __init__(s, o): pass
    def __enter__(s): return s
    def __exit__(s, *a): pass
    def extract_info(s, u, download=False): return dict(title='t', automatic_captions={'en':[dict(ext='vtt', url='u')]})
class _Mod: YoutubeDL = _YDL
class _R: status=200; body=_vtt.encode()
_old = (globals()['_ytdl'], globals()['http_get'], globals()['_yt_index'])
_c = {}
try:
    globals().update(_ytdl=lambda: _Mod, http_get=lambda u: _R, _yt_index=lambda: _c)
    a = read_yt('aircAruvnKk')
    assert 'cues' not in a and a['source'].startswith('hello and welcome')
    b = read_yt('aircAruvnKk', cues=True)
    test_eq(b['cues'], cues); test_eq(b['source'], a['source'])
    assert 'cues' in _c['aircAruvnKk']
    _c['aircAruvnKk'].pop('cues')  # an old cache entry has no cues: refetch
    test_eq(read_yt('aircAruvnKk', cues=True)['cues'], cues)
    globals().update(http_get=lambda u: type('R',(),dict(status=404,body=b''))())
    e = read_yt('aircAruvnKk', cues=True, force=True)
    test_eq((e['source'], e['cues']), ('', []))
finally: globals().update(_ytdl=_old[0], http_get=_old[1], _yt_index=_old[2])
```

## One function for every source

[`read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read) accepts
every kind of target the readers above handle and returns the same seven
fields for all of them: `ok`, `kind`, `title`, `source`, `text`,
`skipped` and `meta`. A program can treat web pages, PDFs, arXiv papers,
YouTube videos, GitHub content and local files alike.

[`what_is`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#what_is)
decides which reader a target needs. A path that exists on disk wins
over every URL rule, so a local file named `pdf` is read from disk
rather than fetched. A GitHub URL containing `/blob/` is one file
(`ghfile`) rather than a whole repository (`github`). Any other http or
https URL is a web page. A failed read returns `ok=False` with the
reason in `skipped`. Only a target that is none of these kinds raises
`ValueError`.

[`what_is`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#what_is)
reads the host of a URL to find arXiv and YouTube links, not the full
text of the URL. `https://docs.example.dev/youtube.com-guide` is a web
page, not a YouTube video.

## Fetching untrusted URLs

A program that reads links from web pages, documents or messages fetches
URLs that another person can choose. For these URLs, call
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch),
[`get_pdf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_pdf) and
[`read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read) with
`auto=False`. fossick then uses only plain HTTP. It checks and pins each
address, and checks each redirect again. `max_bytes` can limit the size
of each download.

The tests below use a small web server in this process, on 127.0.0.1.
The address check refuses 127.0.0.1, so `_public_loopback` makes the
check count it as public for the length of a test. The server can then
act as a site on the internet. `_public_loopback` can also give a name
an address that only the check sees. libcurl does not see that address.

Any page can contain the proof-of-work markers that
[`get_pdf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_pdf)
looks for. Here the page contains them, and the answer gets a redirect
to `localhost`.
[`get_pdf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_pdf)
refuses the redirect. The server log shows that the request to `/secret`
was not sent.

``` python
_Site.hits.clear()
with _public_loopback(): test_fail(lambda: get_pdf(f'{_base}/paper.pdf'), contains='localhost is an internal host')
test_eq(_Site.hits, ['/paper.pdf', '/paper.pdf'])   # the answer was sent; the redirect to /secret was not followed
```

fossick checks a redirect by the address that its host resolves to, not
only by its name. Here `inside.invalid` resolves to 10.0.0.7, so fossick
refuses the redirect. The second fetch tests the pin. Names that end in
`.invalid` never resolve in real DNS. The fetch can reach the server
only through the address that the check approved and gave to libcurl.

``` python
_Site.hits.clear()
with _public_loopback({'inside.invalid': '10.0.0.7'}):
    test_fail(lambda: fetch(f'{_base}/to-inside'), contains='resolves to 10.0.0.7')
with _public_loopback({'pinned.invalid': '127.0.0.1'}):
    r = fetch(f'http://pinned.invalid:{_srv.server_port}/page')
test_eq(r.status, 200)
test_eq(_Site.hits, ['/to-inside', '/page'])
```

`max_bytes` stops a large body. The server sends 4 MB with no
`Content-Length`.
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch) and
[`get_pdf`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#get_pdf)
stop after 100,000 bytes and raise
[`TooLarge`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#toolarge).
With no `max_bytes`, the download is not limited, as before.

``` python
test_fail(lambda: fetch(f'{_base}/big', allow_private=True, max_bytes=100_000, retries=1), contains='max_bytes=100000')
test_fail(lambda: get_pdf(f'{_base}/big', allow_private=True, max_bytes=100_000, retries=1), contains='max_bytes=100000')
with _public_loopback(): test_fail(lambda: fetch(f'{_base}/big', max_bytes=100_000, retries=1), contains='max_bytes')
test_eq(len(fetch(f'{_base}/big', allow_private=True).body), 64 * 65536)   # no limit unless one is asked for
```

A CA bundle from `SSL_CERT_FILE` is used on each request. The test
starts an HTTPS server with a self-signed certificate, made with the
`openssl` command. Without the bundle, the certificate check fails. With
`SSL_CERT_FILE` set to the certificate, or with `ca_bundle=`, the
download works. `verify=True` stays on in each case.

``` python
import ssl, tempfile
_td = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
subprocess.run(['openssl', 'req', '-x509', '-newkey', 'rsa:2048', '-nodes', '-days', '1', '-subj', '/CN=127.0.0.1',
                '-addext', 'subjectAltName=IP:127.0.0.1', '-keyout', str(_td/'key.pem'), '-out', str(_td/'cert.pem')],
               check=True, capture_output=True, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
_tls = ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), _Site)
_ctx = ssl.create_default_context(ssl.Purpose.CLIENT_AUTH); _ctx.load_cert_chain(_td/'cert.pem', _td/'key.pem')
_tls.socket = _ctx.wrap_socket(_tls.socket, server_side=True)
threading.Thread(target=_tls.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
_https = f'https://127.0.0.1:{_tls.server_port}/notes.txt'

_env = {v: os.environ.pop(v) for v in ('SSL_CERT_FILE', 'CURL_CA_BUNDLE', 'REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE') if v in os.environ}
try:
    test_fail(lambda: http_get(_https, allow_private=True, retries=1), contains='(60)')
    test_eq(http_get(_https, allow_private=True, retries=1, ca_bundle=_td/'cert.pem').body, b'secret')
    os.environ['SSL_CERT_FILE'] = str(_td/'cert.pem')
    test_eq(http_get(_https, allow_private=True, retries=1).body, b'secret')
    with _public_loopback(): test_eq(fetch(_https, verify=True, retries=1).body, b'secret')   # the pinned path too
finally:
    os.environ.pop('SSL_CERT_FILE', None); os.environ.update(_env)
    _tls.shutdown(); _tls.server_close()
```

On macOS,
[`_system_ca`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#_system_ca)
makes the CA bundle from certifi’s roots and the output of
`security find-certificate`. The first test gives it a fake `security`
command, so it runs on every system. The bundle holds the certifi roots
and the fake certificate. A fresh file is used again without a new
`security` call. When `security` gives no certificate,
[`_system_ca`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#_system_ca)
keeps the old file. Off macOS,
[`_system_ca`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#_system_ca)
returns None and curl uses its own roots.

``` python
from unittest.mock import patch
import certifi, tempfile
```

``` python
_fake_pem = '-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\nZmFrZQ==\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n'
_calls = []
def _fake_run(cmd, **kw):
    _calls.append(cmd)
    return subprocess.CompletedProcess(cmd, 0, _fake_pem if cmd[0] == 'security' else '', '')
_ca = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'ca.pem'
with patch.object(sys, 'platform', 'darwin'), patch('subprocess.run', _fake_run):
    test_eq(_system_ca(_ca), str(_ca))
    test_eq(_calls[0][:4], ['security', 'find-certificate', '-a', '-p'])
    txt = _ca.read_text()
    assert txt.startswith(Path(certifi.where()).read_text()) and txt.endswith(_fake_pem)
    _system_ca(_ca); test_eq(len(_calls), 1)                 # a fresh file is used again
    _fake_pem = ''
    test_eq(_system_ca(_ca, max_age=0), str(_ca))            # no certificates: keep the old file
    test_eq(_system_ca(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'none.pem'), None)
with patch.object(sys, 'platform', 'linux'): test_eq(_system_ca(_ca), None)
```

On a Mac, the real bundle holds many certificates, and
[`_verify`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#_verify)
gives it to curl when no CA variable is set. Verification stays on.

``` python
if sys.platform == 'darwin':
    _env = {v: os.environ.pop(v) for v in _CA_ENV if v in os.environ}
    try:
        _p = _verify()
        test_eq(_p, _system_ca())
        assert Path(_p).read_text().count('BEGIN CERTIFICATE') > 100
        test_eq(_verify(False), False)                        # verify=False still means off, as before
    finally: os.environ.update(_env)
```

With `auto=False`, no path starts a browser or connects to the debug
Chrome. The test replaces the browser loaders, and the `fossick.cdp`
functions that connect to port 9223, with functions that record each
call. It then runs
[`fetch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#fetch),
[`read`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#read) for a web
page and for PDFs, the proof-of-work step,
[`crawl`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#crawl) and
[`read_gh_file`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/cli.html#read_gh_file).
One of the pages is a bot wall. No call is recorded. As a control,
`fetch(auto=True)` on the same bot wall calls both.

``` python
import fossick.cdp as _cdp
_touched = []
def _no_browser(*a, **k): _touched.append('browser'); raise BrowserUnavailable('no browser in this test')
def _no_cdp(*a, **k): _touched.append('cdp'); raise RuntimeError('no debug Chrome in this test')
_saved = _browser_fetchers, browser_session, _cdp.cdp_ws, _cdp.cdp_cookies, _cdp.cdp_connect
_browser_fetchers = browser_session = _no_browser
_cdp.cdp_ws = _cdp.cdp_cookies = _cdp.cdp_connect = _no_cdp
try:
    with _public_loopback():
        test_eq(fetch(f'{_base}/wall').status, 403)
        assert not read(f'{_base}/wall', auto=False).ok
        assert not read(f'{_base}/wall/doc.pdf', auto=False).ok
        test_fail(lambda: read(f'{_base}/paper.pdf', auto=False), contains='internal host')
        test_eq(len(crawl(f'{_base}/page', max_pages=3)), 1)
        test_eq(read_gh_file(f'{_base}/notes.txt'), 'secret')
        test_eq(_touched, [])
        _r = fetch(f'{_base}/wall', auto=True)   # the control: auto=True does try the browsers and the debug Chrome
finally: _browser_fetchers, browser_session, _cdp.cdp_ws, _cdp.cdp_cookies, _cdp.cdp_connect = _saved
test_eq(_r.tier, 'blocked')
assert {'browser', 'cdp'} <= set(_touched), _touched
_srv.shutdown(); _srv.server_close()
```

    fossick: no browser in this test

## Installing the agent skill

fossick includes a `SKILL.md` that tells coding agents how to use it.
[`mv_skill_md`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#mv_skill_md)
copies it into `.agents/skills/fossick/` at the root of the current git
repository, which
[`repo_root`](https://vedicreader.github.io/fossick/core.html#repo_root)
finds. It also copies it into `.claude/skills/fossick/` under the
working directory. With `dry_run=True`, the default, it prints where the
file would go and copies nothing. The `fossick install` command copies
the file.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick/blob/main/fossick/core.py#L1238"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


print where it would go when `dry_run` is True.*


``` python
root = repo_root()
assert root is not None and (root/'.git').exists(), f"Expected git root, got {root}"
mv_skill_md(dry_run=True)
```

``` python
for _bad in ('http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/',
             'http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin', 'http://localhost/x', 'http://10.0.0.5/x',
             'http://192.168.1.1/', 'http://[::1]/', 'http://metadata.google.internal/',
             'http://0.0.0.0/', 'file:///etc/passwd'):
    try: check_url(_bad); raise SystemExit(f'not blocked: {_bad}')
    except BlockedURL: pass

assert check_url('https://example.com/a') == 'https://example.com/a'
assert check_url('http://127.0.0.1:8000/x', allow_private=True)

# a BlockedURL message names the override, or callers remove the address check
try: check_url('http://localhost/x')
except BlockedURL as e: assert 'allow_private' in str(e) and 'FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE' in str(e)

os.environ['FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE'] = '1'
try: assert check_url('http://127.0.0.1/x')
finally: del os.environ['FOSSICK_ALLOW_PRIVATE']
```
